info.title: Daymaker API
info.description:
Daymaker API. Base URL: https://daymaker.com/api/v2. Key prefixes: dmk_live_ and dmk_test_. Docs: https://daymaker.com/api/v2/docs. OpenAPI: https://daymaker.com/api/v2/openapi.json.
Cold Caked Cake API keys use dm_live_ or dm_test_ and belong at https://daymaker.com/api/v1/partner. For those keys read https://coldcaked.com/docs/api and https://daymaker.com/api/v1/partner/openapi.json. Key families are not interchangeable; never change a key's prefix.
Daymaker from your own server: leads and research, gift ideas and picks, campaigns, sending (gift links, payment pages, Reach out), orders, the pipeline and signals.

A key acts as the person who made it: their role, their team, their credits and their limits, exactly as in the Daymaker app. Make keys in Daymaker under Settings, API and MCP. Keep them on a server: a key in a browser or an app is a key anyone can use.

Customer keys (dmk_live_) can expire after 30, 90, or 365 days, or have no expiry. Daymaker staff can only make test keys (dmk_test_): read-only access to the real workspace and prices, expiring 7 days after creation. Test keys cannot make changes, spend credits, or send gifts or messages. GET /me returns key.test and key.expires_at (null when no expiry was chosen). An expired key returns 401.

Scopes: `read`: See your workspace: leads, campaigns, orders, the pipeline and signals, each lead's gift link, and prices before anything is sent. `work`: Add leads, start research and gift searches (these use credits), pick gifts, write notes and change campaigns. `send`: Send gift links, make payment pages, reach out by email and LinkedIn, and post public replies to signals, all in your name.

Errors are `{ "error": { "code", "message", "request_id", ... } }`. Branch on the HTTP status and `code`; `message`, `next` and `why` are words for people and may change. Lists take `limit` (1 to 100, default 25) and `offset`, and answer `total` and `next_offset` (null at the end); a page can hold fewer than `limit` (`cut_short: true`), so continue from `next_offset`. Query values: numbers as digits, booleans as true or false, each field once. Bodies are JSON objects sent with `Content-Type: application/json` (any other type is answered 415), at most 1 MB; unknown body fields, at any depth, are refused. Every request counts against 120 a minute per key and 240 a minute per person.

apiKey.description: Authorization: Bearer <key> (X-Api-Key also works). Make a key in Daymaker under Settings, API and MCP. Customer keys use dmk_live_ and can expire after 30, 90, or 365 days, or have no expiry; staff can only make read-only dmk_test_ keys that expire 7 days after creation.

code.description: What went wrong, for code to branch on. Fix the request: validation_error, bad_request, unsupported_media_type, payload_too_large, method_not_allowed, idempotency_mismatch (use a new key). Key: unauthenticated (make or check the key), insufficient_scope (a key with that scope). Stop and tell the person: forbidden, forbidden_role (an owner or admin pays), not_let_in, not_found, refused, missing_details, not_priceable, nobody_added, over_max_credits, insufficient_credits, too_many_for_today, possible_match (what_to_do says the way on), already_researched_recently, nothing_to_pay, conflict (something else is under way), not_done (cancelled or failed: the message says which), held (ask Daymaker). Re-quote: quote_changed. Wait, then retry (the same Idempotency-Key may be sent again): idempotency_in_flight, rate_limited, daily_limit, paused, not_available_here, service_unavailable. Check, then decide: in_progress (POST /purchases/{purchase_id}/sync gives the payment page once it is ready; send again only if none is open), outcome_unknown and partially_done (check what was done; a new request needs a new Idempotency-Key). Ours: internal_error, bad_gateway.

message.description: What went wrong, in words for people.

request_id.description: Quote it when asking Daymaker about this request.

fields.description: With validation_error: each field that needs a look.

needs.description: With insufficient_scope: the scope the key lacks.

reason.description: The app's own reason, when it gave one.

new_quote.description: With quote_changed: the price now. Check it with the person, then send again with its quote_revision.

missing.description: With missing_details: what each lead still needs.

left_out.description: Leads that could not be priced, and why.

purchase_id.description: With in_progress, outcome_unknown or nothing_to_pay: the purchase it is about.

research_starts_left.description: With too_many_for_today: how many research runs can still start today.

link.description: The Daymaker page where the same thing lives.

each.description: With a Reach out quote_changed: each lead's price now.

total_if_all_say_yes_usd.description: With a Reach out quote_changed: the total to send again with.

index.description: With nobody_added: the place in the list you sent.

skipped.description: With refused or nobody_added: who was left out, and why.

state.description: With in_progress or held: where the payment page is.

liked.description: With partially_done: the like went up.

replied.description: With partially_done: the comment did not.

next.description: What to do next, in words for people.

E400.description: The request is malformed or a field is wrong (`validation_error` lists them in `fields`), or the body is not JSON (`bad_request`).

E401.description: No key, or a key that is not valid (revoked, unknown, an expired key, or its account is deleted, banned, or has no verified primary email address).

E403.description: The key lacks the scope (`insufficient_scope`), the person's role cannot do this (`forbidden_role`, `forbidden`), or the account is not let in yet (`not_let_in`).

E404.description: No such lead, campaign, purchase or signal in this workspace.

E409.description: The state moved: the price changed (`quote_changed`), a payment page is still being made (`in_progress`), work is already under way (`conflict`), research may have found someone else (`possible_match`), research ran recently (`already_researched_recently`), nothing waits for payment (`nothing_to_pay`), it is held (`held`), it did not happen (`not_done`), or the first request with this Idempotency-Key is still running (`idempotency_in_flight`).

E415.description: The body is not JSON sent with `Content-Type: application/json` (`unsupported_media_type`).

E422.description: Understood but not done: over `max_credits`, a lead misses what this way of sending needs (`missing_details`), nothing could be priced (`not_priceable`), nobody could be added (`nobody_added`), more research than today allows (`too_many_for_today`), Daymaker refused it (`refused`), or the Idempotency-Key was used for another request or workspace authority (`idempotency_mismatch`).

E429.description: Over a limit: requests per minute or hour (`rate_limited`) or a day's research runs or gift searches (`daily_limit`). See Retry-After.

E500.description: Something went wrong in Daymaker (`internal_error`). Try again, and quote the request_id if it keeps happening.

E502.description: A change began and Daymaker could not confirm how it ended (`outcome_unknown`: check before trying again), part of it was done (`partially_done`), or a service Daymaker relies on failed (`bad_gateway`).

E503.description: Paused for maintenance (`paused`), not available on this server (`not_available_here`), or not available just now (`service_unavailable`). See Retry-After.

get.description:
Who the key acts as and what they can do: email, role (owner, admin or member; only owners and admins can pay), credits and the monthly plan, the workspace's gift budget range, and the gift categories the team never wants suggested. Free.

Scope: `read`.

never_suggest.description: Gift categories the team never wants suggested.

never_suggest_unavailable.description: True when the team's gift rules could not be read just now: ask the person, or try again.

test.description: True for a test key (dmk_test_): it only reads, and stops working at expires_at.

expires_at.description: When the key stops working. Null when no expiry was chosen for a live key. Staff test keys stop within 7 days of creation.

get.description:
The workspace's leads, your own first. `tab` narrows them as the Leads page's tabs do. `updated_since` keeps only the leads edited at or after that time (ISO 8601, such as 2026-11-01T09:00:00Z; send a zone's + as %2B). `note` says when the workspace has more leads than one read holds; a campaign's own list (GET /campaigns/{campaign_id}) then has all of its people.

Scope: `read`.

parameters.description: Only leads in this campaign (GET /api/v2/campaigns).

parameters.description: Only leads edited at or after this time: an ISO 8601 date and time with its zone, such as 2026-11-01T09:00:00Z. A lead with no time at all is left out.

post.description:
Adds up to 50 people to a campaign (or the Unfiled list when campaign_id is left out). The same person twice, or a person already in the campaign, is not added again. `research: true` starts research for each new lead after the answer, one at a time, 37.5 credits each; `max_credits` refuses the call, spending nothing, when that could cost more. 201 when someone was added.

Scope: `work`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Any unique string, such as a UUID, at most 255 visible characters. Once a request with this key has done something, a retry with the same key gets that first answer (with Idempotent-Replay: true) instead of doing it again. An answer that changed nothing (a refusal, a limit, a price that moved) is not kept, so the same key may be sent again. Kept 24 hours per API key. Each retry checks current app access and is bound to the original identity, team, role and key scopes. Changed access or an older unbound record cannot replay; a changed authority returns 422 idempotency_mismatch. Check the original action before using a new key.

research.description: starting when research was asked for.

link_not_kept.description: A linkedin_url that is not a LinkedIn profile was not kept: research reads only their name and company.

not_read.description: People past the first 50, not read.

The `why` of a gift is for the sender only: never put it in a note.

Scope: `read`.

total_usd.description: What checkout charges for it, fees included: our hub's shipping is priced to where they are (their address, else their state, else the US average).

price.description: The price as shown, for example $89.00.

fees_usd.description: What the fees in total_usd cover: the sales tax; the shipping to the recipient, USPS from our hub or the store's own for a gift it ships straight to them; and Daymaker's repackaging and service. A price quoted before those were told apart has its fees as shipping_and_repackaging alone.

general.description: A general gift rather than a personal one.

gift_link.description: Their gift link: the link you share with them yourself, whole (https://), while it can still be claimed. Made by POST /campaigns/{campaign_id}/gift-links with share_link, by POST /campaigns/{campaign_id}/reach-out with the link channel (or X, or a LinkedIn message you send yourself), or the same in the app. Left out when there is none, when only Daymaker sends it (its email, your connected LinkedIn), once it closed, was claimed or was withdrawn, and for someone who asked not to get gift invites. When the same offer also goes out by Daymaker's email, that email carries this link too. Each link opens that person's gift only.

gift_link_unavailable.description: True when the gift links could not be read just now, so a missing gift_link may still exist: try again shortly.

on_lead.description: The lead the reply came in on.

reply.description: Their reply on LinkedIn to a gift offer: when, the address it gave, and the offer it answered.

link.description: The Daymaker page where the same thing lives.

post.description:
Starts research on a lead: 37.5 credits (one search), usually about an hour; the person who started it gets an email when it lands. 202 when this call started it (`started: true`). 200 with `started: false` when nothing new started: research is already running or in, an earlier call is starting it, or research Daymaker already had came back at once. `charged_credits` is what this call spent, when known: 0 when nothing was charged, 37.5 when research came back at once at the usual price (copied in from outside your team, or a run that finished at once), null when not known yet. 409 `possible_match` when research found someone who may be this lead, and nothing was started or charged: `what_to_do` says the way on (if it is the same person, their research is on another lead: find it with GET /leads?search=; if not, add them again with their `linkedin_url`, then research them). Poll GET /leads/{lead_id} (`research.state`) for the result.

Scope: `work`.

post.description:
Offers each lead their gift in your name, on the `channels` you give (email, linkedin, x, link); left out, email and LinkedIn where those are on file. Explicit x or link returns words and a gift link in `send_by_hand` for you to share; this endpoint never sends an X message. Emails go at once, or are handed to your team's Nooks sequence when enabled; LinkedIn at LinkedIn's pace, within its daily and weekly limits. LinkedIn messages that cannot go out (not connected, or signed out by LinkedIn) also come back in `send_by_hand`. `sent_to` includes leads reached on at least one channel or handed to Nooks; a Nooks hand-off does not confirm delivery (POST /purchases/{purchase_id}/sync names the sequence). `later` goes after its warm note or at LinkedIn's pace, and a LinkedIn message comes back for you to send by hand if LinkedIn signs you out first. A yes waits for an owner or admin to pay (POST /purchases/{purchase_id}/checkout) and is never charged on its own. `total_usd` must be the quote's `total_if_all_say_yes_usd`. Messages cannot be recalled.
